name: manual_168731
claim: Supersedes the "rule cannot be located" claim in lesson_9bcca08eefa4, lesson_4a711949b3ed, lesson_e0ff7f2d6717, and lesson_1079e8c74f20 -- all four repeated a search failure across multiple turns (checked orama-system's CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .coderabbit.yaml only) and never checked .cursor/rules/, a standard Cursor IDE rule-file location that should have been checked from the first search, not the fourth attempt. The rule genuinely exists: orama-system/.cursor/rules/common-coding-style.mdc, frontmatter "alwaysApply: true" (global, not path-scoped), verbatim: "ALWAYS create new objects, NEVER mutate existing ones" with the contrasting pseudocode example modify(original, field, value) -> changes original in-place [WRONG] vs update(original, field, value) -> returns new copy with change [CORRECT]. Stated rationale: "Immutable data prevents hidden side effects, makes debugging easier, and enables safe concurrency." This directly, unambiguously governs MiniGraph.add_node/add_edge, which lesson_1079e8c74f20 reverted to mutating self and returning self on the (mistaken) premise that no such rule existed to conflict with real LangGraph compatibility evidence. The LangGraph-compatibility evidence itself remains correct and unaffected (8/8 real-world sources use bare, non-reassigned add_node calls) -- what changed is that the rule conflict is now confirmed real, not hypothetical, and must be resolved against verified, real constraints on both sides rather than one side being falsely absent.

decisions.notes: Direct operator correction locating the exact rule file after four prior failed search attempts -- the rule is real and must supersede the false-absence claim across all four prior lessons that repeated it.
